# Damage over Time — skill-DoT damage model

- **Status:** 🔶 Partial
- **Skills affected:** Mind Control, Path of Flames
- **Mechanic tags:** dot, damage-pool, tick-rounding, methodology
- **Last verified:** 2026-07-10 by Tyra

## Setup

SS12. Skill level 16, no gear unless stated. Target: the standard Level-85 dummy (30% erosion resistance, 30% elemental resistance, 50% armor) — see [training-dummy](training-dummy.md). Two skills, both `Spell / Channeled / Persistent`, 2s Damage Over Time, cast speed 0.333: **Mind Control** (Erosion, base 222/sec at L16) and **Path of Flames** (Fire, base 299/sec at L16). "Meter" = the in-game damage-recount readout (span average, not the tooltip — see [training-dummy](training-dummy.md) methodology note).

## Raw data points

Model vs meter, twelve parses (model error in parens):

- Mind Control, baseline: 155.4 → 150.5 (+3.3%)
- Mind Control, +18% Skill Effect Duration: 155.4 → 150.0 (+3.6%)
- Mind Control, +9% increased: 169.4 → 180.0 (−5.9%)
- Mind Control, +27% increased: 197.4 → 210.0 (−6.0%)
- Mind Control, Control Spell (+35.5% additional): 210.6 → 210.5 (0.0%)
- Mind Control, Shortened Duration (+27.5% additional): 198.1 → 210.0 (−5.6%)
- Mind Control, Shortened Duration + 18% Skill Effect Duration: 198.1 → 209.0 (−5.2%)
- Path of Flames, baseline: 209.3 → 210.0 (−0.3%)
- Path of Flames, +9% increased: 228.1 → 240.5 (−5.1%)
- Path of Flames, +27% increased DoT: 265.8 → 269.0 (−1.2%)
- Path of Flames, Control Spell, standing still: 283.6 → 301.0 (−5.8%)
- Path of Flames, Control Spell + 18% increased: 334.6 → 330.0 (+1.4%)

Worst-case model error is **−6.0% / +3.6%**.

## Derived / confirmed formula

`dot_dps = base_per_second(level) × (1 + Σ increased) × Π(1 + additional) × resist_only_mult`, where `resist_only_mult` applies ONLY the target's resistance (no armor term — see [dot-armor-exclusion](dot-armor-exclusion.md)). Order of operations confirmed by the Path of Flames "Control Spell + 18% increased" parse: `209.3 × 1.18 × 1.355 = 334.6` matches the meter (330.0) far better than applying the additional term first.

## Notes / caveats / open questions

**Partial — the residual is unexplained.** Ship with a disclaimer of "may be off by up to ~10%" (a widened safety margin for untested magnitudes; the measured worst case here is 6.0%).

The residual is ~0% with no damage mods and with additional-only mods; it is ~+6% (meter above model) whenever *increased* damage is present. It is NOT pulse damage (frame-by-frame video analysis at 60fps shows pulse damage scaling exactly with the mod: 5.0/tick baseline → 5.5/tick at +9%, a ratio of 1.10), NOT cadence (61-frame pulse period, identical with and without the mod, sd 2.28 frames), and NOT a second damage source (no second damage-number stream anywhere on screen).

The residual behaves like a **constant** multiplicative term, not one proportional to the pools: Mind Control's meter/model ratio was 1.0627 at +9% increased and 1.0641 at +27% increased — a 3× change in the mod moved the ratio only 0.1 pt. All parses in this set use small mods (≤35%); whether the ratio stays constant at build-realistic magnitudes (+150–200% increased) is an OPEN verification item, not established.

**Confirmed, do NOT model:** the in-game `DoT DPS` character-sheet readout computes damage as if a second contained **31** server ticks; a second contains 30. Mind Control baseline: per-tick damage 5.0, sheet reads 155 (`5.0 × 31`), real DPS 150 (`5.0 × 30`). Damage numbers land on a ladder of `per_tick × {29,30,31}` (Mind Control baseline: 145 / 150 / 155). **Path of Flames shows no such offset** (7.0/tick, sheet 209, meter 210 — neither is a clean ×29/×31 rung off 210), so the divisor appears skill-specific, not universal. Applying a blanket 30/31 correction factor takes the worst-case model error from 6.0% to **9.1%** on this dataset — it is therefore deliberately NOT modelled.

Cast speed: no effect on DoT DPS (expected — a Persistent DoT isn't delivered per-cast). Duration: no effect on DPS (tested with +18% Skill Effect Duration alone AND stacked on Shortened Duration). The `Extended Duration` support ("Supports Duration Skills") is socketable onto a Persistent skill but grants nothing measurable here.

`Damage`, `Spell Damage`, and `Damage over Time` increased mods all pool into ONE increased pool (confirmed twice, on both skills).

**Open questions:** the ~6% increased-damage residual and its cause; whether the meter/model ratio stays constant at high magnitudes (test: +150–200% increased on Mind Control, check the ratio stays in 0.96–1.07); why Path of Flames shows no 31-tick sheet offset while Mind Control shows it exactly.

**CONFIRMED — above-max-level scaling is universal across every damage form (Tyra, owner, 2026-07-10):** above-max-level scaling (the compounding ×1.10-per-level multiplier applied past a skill's max level) applies to hit, DoT, secondary, minion, magus, and focus damage — every damage form, with no DoT-specific exception. A level-21 DoT skill (max level 20) resolves as level-20-capped base × 1.10, exactly like a level-21 hit skill: this is a general engine-wide principle, not a per-skill special case. This is an owner statement of an established game mechanic, distinct from the twelve parse-measured data points above, and it resolves the prior open question here in favor of "applies universally," reversing the earlier "deliberately NOT applied, unsourced" stance.

**Engine status: WIRED (2026-07-10).** `compute_dot` (~L1193) now takes an `above_mult: float = 1.0` parameter, multiplied into each form's `dps` before mitigation (so it propagates into `dps_vs_target` too, ~L1281-1285); `calculate_offense`'s call site (~L2519) passes the SAME `above_mult = _above_max_mult(effective_level, skill.max_level)` (~L1833) already computed for the hit stage — one multiplier, shared by both stages, exactly as the owner confirmed. See `.wolf/buglog.json` id `dot-above-max-level-scaling-not-applied`. The ±10% model disclaimer above now covers above-max-level DoT builds like every other damage form. `backend/tests/test_dot.py`'s `TestAboveMaxLevelApplied` pins the corrected value (519.75 = 675 × 1.10 × 0.70) and is green.

**CONFIRMED — the damage-scoping rule (type / elemental), resolving `fire_dot_dmg_inc` (Tyra, owner, 2026-07-10):** an owner statement of the general scoping rule for which "X Damage" mods apply to a DoT, distinct from the twelve parse-measured data points above (which only isolated the generic `Damage`/`Damage over Time` stats, never a type-scoped or Elemental one): (1) "X Damage" (increased or additional) applies to BOTH a hit and an X-type DoT, e.g. Fire Damage scales a fire DoT and fire hits, Erosion Damage scales an erosion DoT; (2) "X Damage over Time" applies to X-type DoT ONLY, which resolves the `fire_dot_dmg_inc` question previously recorded here: "Fire Damage over Time" is now CONFIRMED (not merely inferred) to apply to fire DoTs (Path of Flames); (3) "Elemental Damage" applies to fire/cold/lightning DoTs but NOT erosion, since Elemental excludes Erosion, matching TLI's general Elemental definition; (4) additional pools scope identically to increased.

**Engine status: WIRED (2026-07-10).** `_dot_type_increased_keys`/`_dot_type_additional_keys` (~L158-172, type-generic from `form.dtype`, each key guarded against actually existing in `STAT_META` via `_ALL_STAT_KEYS` so a type lacking a `{T}_dot_dmg_inc` stat is a no-op) plus per-dtype caches `_DOT_TYPE_INCREASED_KEYS`/`_DOT_TYPE_ADDITIONAL_KEYS` (~L186-187, reusing the existing `ELEMENTAL` set — the SAME one `_target_effective` already uses to keep `elemental_pen` off Erosion, so the Elemental-excludes-Erosion definition stays single-sourced). `compute_dot`'s per-form loop (~L1260-1281) unions these into the increased sum by key (`fire_dot_dmg_inc`, already in the static whitelist, is deduped — not double-counted) and multiplies a SECOND, form-scoped additional product over `{type}_dmg_additional` + `elemental_dmg_additional` + `spell_dmg_additional` (spell skills only). `fire_dot_dmg_inc` (~L136 in `_DOT_INCREASED_STATS`) is now CONFIRMED rather than inferred by the rule above. `spell_dmg_additional` is EXCLUDED from the DoT additional pool, not merely unconfirmed-but-included: unlike `spell_dmg_inc` (measured, whitelisted on the increased side), no additional-pool spell-scoped mod was independently isolated in the twelve parses, and "Spell" is a form tag the type/elemental scoping rule above never covers — per the owner's under-compute-and-flag policy the engine leaves it inert pending an in-game measurement (open verification item below). See `.wolf/buglog.json` id `dot-type-scoped-damage-pools-missing` for the verified probe values (e.g. Mind Control +40% erosion_dmg_inc → 217.56, was inert; Path of Flames +40% fire_dmg_inc AND +40% fire_dmg_additional → 410.228, confirming increased/additional are separate multiplicative pools, not summed). `backend/tests/test_dot.py` (`TestTypeScopedDamageApplies`, `TestWhitelistBoundaryNegative`, `TestAboveMaxLevelApplied`) pins all of the above as green. The `mind_control.json` golden fixture's `consumed_stats` gained `erosion_dmg_inc`/`erosion_dmg_additional` entries (no numeric field moved); `path_of_flames.json`'s golden is untouched.

**OPEN verification item — `spell_dmg_additional` on a DoT (unmeasured, excluded by default):** no parse in the twelve-point dataset above and no owner statement establishes whether a Spell-scoped ADDITIONAL stat (e.g. "+X% additional Spell Damage") applies to a skill-DoT's tick — "Spell" is a form tag, not a damage type or Elemental, so it falls outside the type/elemental damage-scoping rule, and the measured increased-side result (`spell_dmg_inc`) doesn't transfer to the additional side (increased and additional were audited independently in this dataset). The engine therefore EXCLUDES `spell_dmg_additional` from the DoT additional pool by default (`backend/engine/offense.py`, ~L178-186) — this is the deliberate conservative default (owner's "under-compute is better than over-compute, flag it" policy), not a bug. In-game test to close this: equip a "+X% additional Spell Damage" source (isolated, no other increased/additional mods active) on a spell skill-DoT (Mind Control or Path of Flames) and check whether the tick's DPS moves by the expected factor. `test_dot.py::TestWhitelistBoundaryNegative::test_spell_dmg_additional_excluded_from_dot_additional_pool` pins the current (correct) excluded behavior.

## Implementation (engine model)

IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-10, whitelist + above-max expanded 2026-07-10 per owner confirmation — see notes): `backend/engine/offense.py::compute_dot(source, skill, lookup_level, is_spell, extra_additional, above_mult=1.0)` (~L1193) is the DoT damage stage — presence-gated on `skill.dot_forms_by_level`, returns `(rows, dot_dps, dot_dps_vs_target)`. `above_mult` (default 1.0, a no-op at/under a skill's max level) is the SAME `_above_max_mult(effective_level, skill.max_level)` `calculate_offense` (~L2519) already computes for the hit stage (~L1833) — multiplied into each form's `dps` before mitigation, so it propagates into `dps_vs_target` too. `dot_dps_vs_target = dot_dps × _target_mitigation_dot(source, dtype)` (~L1285), where `_target_mitigation_dot` (~L618) is the resistance-only sibling of `_target_mitigation` this entry originally anticipated — confirmed no armor term, matching [dot-armor-exclusion](dot-armor-exclusion.md). Increased pool is a hand-picked whitelist, NOT `stat_meta.affects`: the static `_DOT_INCREASED_STATS` (`dmg_inc + dot_dmg_inc` always, `spell_dmg_inc` for spell skills only, `fire_dot_dmg_inc` for fire DoTs only, ~L132-137) UNIONED by key (dedup, no double-count) with the type-generic `_dot_type_increased_keys(form.dtype)` (~L158-166, `{type}_dmg_inc`/`{type}_dot_dmg_inc`/`elemental_dmg_inc` per the owner-confirmed damage-scoping rule) via the per-dtype cache `_DOT_TYPE_INCREASED_KEYS` (~L186) — this is narrower than the generic hit-pool reader by design, since a DoT must not pick up unrelated hit-only increased stats. Additional pool is TWO multiplicative products: the base `dmg_additional` + `dot_dmg_additional` product via the parametrized `_additional_product(source, factors, predicate, keyed_tags=...)` helper (generalized from the old hit-only helper so both stages share code byte-identically for hit skills), TIMES a second form-scoped product over `_dot_type_additional_keys(form.dtype)` (~L169-172, `{type}_dmg_additional`/`elemental_dmg_additional`). `spell_dmg_additional` is explicitly EXCLUDED from both pools (~L178-186, comment above `_DOT_TYPE_INCREASED_KEYS`) — unlike `spell_dmg_inc` (independently measured, whitelisted on the increased side), no measurement or owner statement establishes that a Spell-scoped additional stat applies to a DoT, so per the owner's under-compute-and-flag policy it stays inert pending an in-game measurement (open verification item below), not included-and-flagged. Then the whole additional product is multiplied by the skill's own `extra_additional` (e.g. Mind Control/Path of Flames' per-channeled-stack `IntrinsicAdditional`). `dmg_additional` is confirmed (not merely modeled) to scale DoT damage — the Control Spell isolation described below still holds and is now load-bearing production code, not a forward guess. Wired into `calculate_offense` right after the Spell Ripple stage, before `_finalize_damage_row_pcts`. Skill-side: `backend/engine/skill_resolver.py` adds `DotForm(base_per_second, dtype, duration=0.0)` (~L30) and `ResolvedSkill.dot_forms_by_level: dict[int, list[DotForm]]` (~L146, default empty — every non-DoT skill is byte-identical to before). `_resolve_dot_skill` (~L594) is the shared resolver registering `mind_control` (~L640, base parsed from `progression[*].values.damage`, erosion) and `path_of_flames` (~L649, base parsed from `values.Descript` instead — its `damage` field is empty at every level) — both `hit_forms_by_level={}` (pure DoT host, no hit component at all), `is_spell=True`, `ChanneledSpec(max_stacks=5, behavior="refresh")`, `IntrinsicAdditional(per=0.215, rating_key="max_channeled_stacks_flat", rating_source="stat")` (dormant at base 5 channeled stacks — confirmed no effect until stacks exceed base). Tests: `backend/tests/test_dot.py` (36 tests across 11 classes: `TestAcceptance`, `TestIncreasedPoolHandComputed`, `TestAdditionalPoolHandComputed`, `TestTypeScopedDamageApplies`, `TestWhitelistBoundaryNegative`, `TestResistanceOnlyMitigation`, `TestNonDotSkillsUnaffected`, `TestDotDamageRowShape`, `TestAboveMaxLevelApplied`, `TestIntrinsicAdditionalChanneledStackEngages`, `TestFutureTypeKeyDerivation`) — reproduces all 12 data points below to stated precision, pins the owner-confirmed above-max-level and type/elemental-scoping mechanics, and covers the type-key-derivation helpers for cold/lightning/physical (no DoT skill of these types exists yet). Full backend suite green (2812 passed). Per-support-skill golden fixtures auto-captured additively at `backend/tests/fixtures/support_skill_golden/{mind_control,path_of_flames}.json`. NYI, surfaced but not wired (see `.wolf/memory.md`, 2026-07-10 DoT session note): Mind Control's link-count scaling (3 base + 1/channeled stack) and its two link-scaled supports (`mind_control_concentrate_magnificent`, `mind_control_enthrall_noble`) — would need a numeric `mind_control_links` condition, out of scope for this ship (single-link acceptance number only, links don't multiply single-target DPS per the verified model); `befuddle`/`entice` gate on subsystems that don't exist yet. Routing note preserved from the original draft: a support line phrased `"+X% additional damage for the supported skill"` (e.g. Control Spell) is NOT special-cased in `support_mapper.py`'s conditional-line table — it falls through `map_line` → `map_via_parser` (~L278) → `engine/mod_parser.py::_parse_custom_mod_text`, the authoritative gear/support/talent stat resolver, which assigns it to `dmg_additional`.
